title: The Frog Almost Ate His Cookie?!
description: An original 42-second visual comedy: a tiny otter drops a cookie into a pond, and a mischievous frog turns a rescue into a surprise. No dialogue.
hook: 0.0s: star-shaped cookie flies from an open tin toward a pond; otter lunges; frog suddenly raises a lily pad by 2.4s. Will the cookie survive?
script: A tiny otter accidentally drops a star-shaped cookie into a pond. A frog tries to catch it on a lily pad, but the cookie bounces away. The otter chases along a slippery dock, nearly catches it, and is blinded by a wind-flipped raincoat hood. The frog pole-vaults with a reed, snatches the cookie and opens its mouth; the otter fears it will eat the snack. Instead, the frog unfolds a hidden red leaf as a clean tray and uses a clam shell to split the rescued cookie equally. The two share a bite, laugh at a silly bubble hiccup, and a second cookie tumbles from the tin in the exact opening framing.

character_bible.otter: One very small caramel-brown river otter with cream cheeks, dark round eyes, short whiskers and a bright yellow raincoat with oversized hood; same fur markings, clothing and proportions in every scene.
character_bible.frog: One tiny emerald-green tree frog with pale throat, large amber eyes and a soft blue cap. A folded crimson leaf is tucked behind the cap until scene 6. Same size and cap throughout.
character_bible.props: Two distinct star-shaped golden oat cookies (first rescued and divided, second appears only in final shot), one small sky-blue metal lunch tin, one smooth clam shell, one folded crimson leaf, one flexible reed.
character_bible.world: Single geographically coherent shallow forest pond beside a weathered wooden dock; three broad lily pads, cattails on far bank, soft afternoon light and gentle ripples. All shots share the same positions and sun direction.
character_bible.style: Original high-end tactile 3D animation, expressive faces, fluid contact physics, bright family-friendly comedy, crisp subject silhouettes, shallow cinematic depth of field, no text/logos/watermarks.
